question.text: If the solution of the differential equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mfenced separators="|"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfenced><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mfenced separators="|"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfenced><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></math> is <math><mn>2</mn><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></math> ( where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is an arbitrary constant), then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
The given equation is
y3⋅3x2cos⁡x3dx+sin⁡x33y2dy=xdx
⇒dsinx3⋅y3=xdx
On integrating, we get,
sin⁡x3⋅y3=x22+C
⇒k=3.
